Hi Sanjay,

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier today. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the core requirements we'll use to size the private deployment and surface the items we need ACME to confirm before we do a formal BOM and SOW. High level: air-gapped VPC-like private cluster, strict tenant isolation (multiple customer namespaces), and 99.9% inferred inference SLA with burst capacity for nightly batch jobs.

Quick checklist for your team to confirm:
- Expected steady-state concurrent inference QPS and 99th pctl latency targets (tokens/s or calls/s).
- Number of tenants (logical customers) to isolate within the cluster initially and expected growth over 12 months.
- Whether you have a preferred block storage vendor (Ceph/Rook, NetApp, Dell/Isilon, or local SAN) or must use in-house SAN.
- KMS choice for disk encryption (customer-managed KMS/HSM) and whether network connections to KMS are allowed from the cluster.
- Procurement timeline for servers (lead times for GPUs/SSDs) and any strict asset tagging/serial tracking needs.

Attached is a lightweight preflight spreadsheet (onprem-preflight-checklist.xlsx) and a quick storage sizer we use to estimate PV capacity. Please fill the shaded inputs and return by EOD next Wednesday if possible.

Notes on our side (so you know constraints):
- We recommend separating node pools: infra (control-plane + logging/monitoring), inference (GPU-backed), and worker (cpu/burst for preprocessing).
- For inference node storage we typically prefer local NVMe for model cache + remote persistent volumes for model artifacts.
- We support customer-managed KMS integration for LUKS-level disk encryption.

Next step: once you return the spreadsheet we'll produce a BOM and a short procurement playbook (preferred SKUs, tolerances).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Ben,

Appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers from our ops/infra side below — I'm copying Maria from EdgeHost (our integrator) who will handle hardware procurement and rack stuffing.

- QPS: Steady-state expected ~180 calls/s (short responses), spike up to 900 calls/s during payroll windows. 99th pctl latency target: <350ms.
- Tenants: Start with 6 logical tenants (finance products), plan to onboard 2 more per quarter.
- Storage: We prefer using our in-house SAN (Dell Unity) for persistent volumes. EdgeHost will evaluate Rook/Ceph if Dell can't meet performance/replication SLA.
- KMS: Must use our customer-managed Vault HSM. Network egress to Vault is allowed via dedicated management VLAN.
- Procurement: GPU lead times are 8-12 weeks (A100-equivalent). We have on-prem procurement window the week of Nov 1; any BOM should be finalized before then.

Also: we expect formal asset tagging and a CSV of serials, MACs, and rack position at delivery.

Next ask: Maria, can you confirm whether the Dell Unity arrays can present block with CSI driver compatibility for dynamic provisioning? If not, recommend a fallback architecture with Ceph+RBD.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Cloud Ops, Acme Payments

On Fri, Oct 15, 2027 at 11:05 AM dev.patel@redwood.ai wrote:
> Ben — adding a more prescriptive ops recommendation to unblock procurement and infra design.

Team,

I've sketched a recommended configuration that balances performance, isolation, and procurement realities. Highlights below and a short BOM section at the end.

1) Node pools (minimum to start):
- control-plane (3x m6-like instances, no GPUs) — dedicated etcd and control plane; host kube-system components and central logging to reduce noisy-tenant noise.
- infra-workers (3x r5-like) — logging, metrics, registry mirror, Bastion, and sidecar proxies.
- inference-gpu (6x GPU nodes initially) — 1/2 GPU density if you need high concurrency per node; use 1x A100-eq per node for predictable latency.
- batch-cpu (2x) — nightly model conversion and offline batch scoring.

2) Storage approach:
- Model cache (ephemeral): local NVMe SSD on inference nodes (raid0 for throughput) for cached weights and KV cache. This keeps token-level latency low.
- Model artifacts (persistent): present as RBD/LVM from Dell Unity if CSI driver available; otherwise deploy Rook/Ceph on infra-workers with replication factor 3. Avoid NFS for model artifacts (metadata contention).
- PVC policy: use ReadWriteOnce for model artifacts; enforce PodDisruptionBudgets and topologies for availability.
- Log/metrics: forward to the dedicated logging cluster or push to S3-compatible object store in a separate VLAN.

3) Tenant isolation model:
- Namespaces per tenant; admission controller enforces resource quotas and node selectors.
- Use taints/tolerations + node selectors so inference workloads for Tenant A are pinned to a tenant-dedicated pool when needed (we can support soft multi-tenant on the same GPU nodes with strict cgroups/QoS as fallback).
- Network policies enforced via Calico with hostEndpoint rules for management plane only.

4) Security & encryption:
- At-rest encryption via LUKS with keys stored in your Vault HSM. We will integrate with Vault's Transit API for attestation and key rotation.
- Image signing with Cosign and an internal registry mirror; enforce admission via OPA Gatekeeper.

5) Observability / SLOs:
- Token-level tracing requires local KV cache observability; recommend sampling at 1% production traffic for the first 60 days to verify model fallbacks.

Procurement/BOM (starter):
- 6 x GPU nodes: each 1x A100-ish, 512GB RAM, 2x 2TB NVMe (for model cache), 2x 10Gb NICs (bonded), local BMC for automation.
- 3 x infra nodes: 256GB RAM, 8TB HDD or 2x 2TB SSD depending on logging retention needs.
- SAN connectivity: FC/iSCSI headroom and CARP for replication if using Dell Unity.

Action items:
- Maria/EdgeHost: confirm CSI compatibility for Dell Unity by Oct 21.
- Sanjay: fill baseline QPS and tenant growth into the sizer sheet (we need peak IOPS estimates).
- Marissa: if procurement needs a formal SKU list for legal, I can convert this BOM into a line-item table by Oct 18.

Attaching storage-sizer-20271010.csv for quick capacity math.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
